title: Vendor, code-object family and lowering route are three axes, and shared code keeps collapsing them into a target id enumerated by hand

evidence.note: The device survey that separates the axes on one machine: rocminfo reports vendor C-3000 and device type HCU, Triton registers an hcu backend beside amd and selects it, the FP16 dot lowers to v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 rather than any v_mfma, dcc 25.10.0's llc names gfx926/928/936/938 beside the AMD CPUs, and the host installs hy-smi and rocm-smi and no amd-smi -- while the object it emits still carries the amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-- triple. One device, three different answers depending on which axis is being asked about.

The Executor host capture that found two of the instances below: the HIP host contract pinned amd-smi as the device monitor where this host installs rocm-smi and hy-smi, and required a --version probe that rocprof answers with exit 1 and its run banner for --version, -v and --help alike. Both refused the host rather than the tool.

observation: Eight separate repairs in one bring-up, and they are the same defect. Shared code keeps deciding a per-target question by enumerating target ids, and the enumerations disagree about which question they are answering. Measured in this checkout: Target.warp_size was one constant for every target, closed upstream in Compiler v81. warps_per_warpgroup and every vendor-keyed rule read the presence of compute_capability, so a well-formed non-CUDA document was refused in CUDA's words and a fabricated capability pair made it parse with a borrowed 32-lane width. A host declared `kind` for Metal and `runtime_kind` for HIP. The schema v2 Executor identity was a gfx1151 literal, which refuses gfx938 for being the wrong vendor's target when the two differ by vendor and agree on the code object. gfx938 was declared vendor amd on Hygon hardware. evaluation/artifacts.py holds METAL_TARGETS, _CUBIN_TARGETS and AMDGCN_TARGETS -- three frozensets of target ids partitioning all seven targets by code object, read from six sites across evaluation and lab, none of which any Target document can state. The HIP host contract pinned amd-smi as the device monitor and a --version interface that rocprof does not have. Underneath all eight: vendor (who built the hardware), code-object family (what the compiled artifact is) and lowering route (which mechanism emits source) are three independent axes. gfx938 and gfx1151 share a code object and differ by vendor; sm_100a and gfx938 share neither but both reach Triton; apple_gpu_family9 and sm_100a share a lane width and nothing else. Declaring one axis and inferring the rest is what produced every instance above.
proposed_change: Finish what warp_size and vendor started: make the code-object family a declared Target fact, and let the shared layers read it instead of enumerating ids. Concretely, a required Target field naming the object the target's toolchain produces -- cubin, metal_binary_archive, hsaco -- consumed by evaluation/artifacts.py's executable_role and _BUILD_ROLES in place of its three frozensets, and by the metal host, build and observation paths in place of their METAL_TARGETS membership tests. A new target then becomes a document, which is what AGENTS.md's registration rule says it should be, instead of a document plus six edits in Executor-pinned shared code. Leave the Compiler's offline tables alone: cuda_architecture and the AMDGCN route table are deliberate, because offline compilation must not open Target documents in its jail. What they must stop being is a second owner of a fact the document also states -- the route table carries a lane width the Target declares -- and the fix there is for the emitter, which holds the Target, to put that width in the toolchain requirements it already builds, rather than for the jail to look it up. That change alters the requirements contract every retained Triton candidate replays through, so it is sequenced after the declaration and not bundled with it. Until both land, the duplication is at least verified: a contract test holds the offline route's architecture and width against every declared AMDGCN Target document, so adding a target without updating the table fails rather than drifting.
verification_plan: Capacity finding, verified by the absence its change is for: after the declaration lands, adding an eighth Target must require no edit to evaluation/artifacts.py, lab/metal_host.py, lab/metal_build.py, evaluation/metal_observations.py or lab/executor.py, and a neutrality test should assert that by constructing a synthetic target of a fourth vendor and reaching executable_role through the declared field alone. The lane-width half verifies by replaying retained Triton candidates through the successor requirements contract with unchanged compiled artifacts. Neither half claims a device result; both are shared-layer changes whose evidence is a Corpus Gate with unchanged expectations and the existing per-route contracts.
